integrity: The theorem is based on an explicit analytic two-by-two diagonalization, collision asymptotics, Gaussian moment integration, and beta integrals. Diagnostic finite calculations are not presented as proof. Scientific independence has not been established.
scientific_limitations: Two iid uniform one-dimensional nodes, power-exponential kernels with exponent in (0,2], independent Gaussian observation noise, and Lipschitz integrands. Neither multi-node quadrature nor floating-point effects follow. The Gaussian exponent-two specialization is covered by earlier work; the new scope is the roughness-dependent phase transition and sharp all-exponent laws.
title: A roughness threshold and exact noise tails for colliding-node kernel quadrature
